title: Intermediate proxy path split causing burst queuing and streaming timeouts for dedicated customer
text:
Intermediate proxy path split causing burst queuing and streaming timeouts for dedicated customer

description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightFlow reporting intermittent long-tail streaming responses (client-level timeouts ~10-30s) for otherwise healthy request patterns. Problem appears as bursts of queued requests and duplicated TCP handshakes when traffic is routed via an intermediate proxy cluster in us-west; some requests are subsequently proxied to eu-west resulting in extra hop latency and streaming stalls.

Impact:
- Several BrightFlow production endpoints experienced elevated p95/p99 for generative streaming calls starting 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC, lasting in ~2–5 minute bursts every ~30–45 minutes.
- Customer reports UI-level timeouts and partial responses; affect 3 teams and ~1200 monthly requests at peak.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted (dedicated pool for BrightFlow).
- Primary region: us-west-2. Failover path observed into eu-west-1 via intermediate proxy cluster.
- Models: rw-instruct-3b (primary), open-chat-4b (fallback).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send sustained streaming generation workload to BrightFlow account (~30 concurrent streams with short prompts).
2) Observe occasional bursts where initial SYN/handshake completes, then an extra proxy hop is inserted and client sees stalled streaming or 504 after application timeout.
3) Replaying traces shows some requests routed to eu-west even though region affinity remains us-west.

Observed behavior:
- p95/p99 token generation latency increases by 5–20x during bursts.
- TCP connection resets and duplicate TLS handshakes captured in packet traces.
- Router logs show intermittent route score flips and mixed-origin headers (X-Orig-Region: us-west, X-Proxy-Chain: proxy-3 -> proxy-9 -> gateway).

Expected behavior:
- Requests from BrightFlow should remain in pinned us-west dedicated pool unless explicit fallback rules trigger. No cross-region proxying during normal operation.

Logs / Evidence:
- Gateway traces: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/trace-20260312-0345 (partial)
- Router metrics: spike in proxy-queue-length on proxy-9 (us-west) correlated with region-routing decision events.
- Packet capture (redacted): shows TLS renegotiation after an idle timeout between proxy hops.
- Customer ticket thread (Slack): #support-brightflow (link redacted).

comments:
2026-03-12 04:02 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage: escalated to SRE. Observed route flips in gateway logs around 03:20 UTC. Collecting netflow and proxy metrics.
2026-03-12 05:10 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Confirmed queue spikes on proxy-9. Hypothesis: transient load shedding on proxy-3 caused router to recompute path and select eu-west fallback which added hop and caused KV cache mismatch for streaming sessions.
2026-03-12 08:33 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer applied temporary client timeout increase as workaround; they still see UX degradation. We provided them a scoped routing pin to keep traffic in us-west while SRE investigates.
2026-03-13 12:21 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Runbook step: disabled proxy-9 autoscale policy change that was rolling out at the time. Observed reduction in cross-region handoffs in the next 2 hours. Continuing root-cause analysis on scoring logic.
2026-03-14 09:00 - Product: Noted related to recent routing score update PR. PR link: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4987. Coordinating with routing team for a targeted rollback if needed.

investigation_notes:
Findings so far:
- Proxy cluster autoscale and a recent routing score calculation change (weighting of path-cost vs. load) coincided with customer-reported time windows.
- Router occasionally treats proxy-9 as unhealthy briefly, then immediately uses eu-west path; this causes streaming sessions to be proxied mid-session because session affinity keys are stale on the intermediate proxy.
- KV cache (prefix cache) was not warmed on the fallback proxy, causing extra backend cold-start and tokenization delays.
- Reproduced locally with stress test: when proxy A reports borderline load, routing recompute can move ~8–12% of in-flight streams to alternative region, resulting in 2–6s additional handshake and then queuing.

Hypotheses to validate:
1) Routing score update PR increased sensitivity to short-lived load signals; revert or tune thresholds.
2) Proxy health-check TTL policy leading to rapid flapping; increase stability window.
3) Ensure intermediate proxies propagate session-affinity headers and warm KV cache on recipient side before handoff.

resolution:
Workarounds & fixes applied:
- Temporary account-level routing pin enforced for BrightFlow to keep traffic in us-west.
- Rolled back an autoscale policy change on proxy-9 that correlated with the incident window.
- Hotfix applied to routing scoring to reduce over-sensitivity to transient load signals (controlled rollout started 2026-03-14 08:00 UTC).
- Follow-up items: routing team to instrument longer stability windows and add pre-warm handshake to fallback proxies; engineering ticket INT-2210 created to track permanent fixes.

Customer communication:
- Notified customer BrightFlow of interim mitigation and ETA for permanent fix. They validated improved behavior after routing pin applied and reported fewer timeouts. Plan: partner with customer to monitor for 72 hours post-fix.
